# 2026-10-22 — A/B: FLQ vs reference lossless codecs and general archivers

> Era note: this run predates release. "pack"/v3/`--no-joint` refer to the
> removed archive mode (self/cross references); shipped v1 keeps the same
> LPC/Rice + stereo core, replacing references with independent frames.

Commit `e254a5b`. Question: is FLQ's LPC/Rice core competitive with real
lossless codecs, or is its whole win just container + joint refs?

## Method

Corpus: `sample_pack/` — the same freesound author-pack corpus as earlier
sweeps: 148 files (.wav ×142, .aif/.aiff ×6), **1572.2 MiB** of PCM.
Group names (`klankbeeld`, `timbre`, `looplicator`, `cat-fox_alex`,
`newlocknew`, `smkoski02`) are freesound.org uploader names.

Each tool encodes each input **single-file**, then decodes and is verified:

- audio codecs: decoded WAV `data` chunk payload byte-compared against the
  input's (`nochk` where not comparable — AIFF inputs through Monkey's
  Audio, which decodes to WAV and loses the BE→LE mapping);
- archivers + FLQ: decoded file sha256-compared to the input (FLQ keeps
  byte-exact file identity).

All successful outputs verified **exact** — zero corruption in any tool.

| Tool | Version | Settings |
|---|---|---|
| FLQ | e254a5b | `flq encode in out.flq` |
| FLAC | 1.5.0 win64 | `-8 -j8` |
| WavPack | 5.9.0 win64 | `-hx` |
| OptimFROG | 5.100 x64 | `--mode extranew-light --optimize fast --aca` |
| TAK | 2.3.3 | `-e -p4m` |
| Monkey's Audio | 13.42 x64 | `-c4000 -threads=4` |
| 7-Zip | 26.05 | `a -t7z -mx=9 -m0=LZMA2` |
| Zstd | 1.5.7 | `--ultra -22 -T0` |
| PAQ8PX | v214 | `-8`, subset only (every 15th file, ≤4 MiB → n=7) |

## Headline: identical files only (n = 47)

Files **every** tool accepted — the honest apples-to-apples cut:

| Tool | ratio | median |
|---|---|---|
| OptimFROG | **48.40%** | 50.06% |
| TAK | **49.88%** | 51.12% |
| **FLQ** | **50.51%** | 51.13% |
| Monkey's Audio | 50.85% | 52.70% |
| FLAC | 51.15% | 52.64% |
| WavPack | 52.04% | 53.60% |
| 7-Zip LZMA2 | 64.60% | 62.38% |
| Zstd | 78.08% | 82.23% |

FLQ beats FLAC (−0.6 pp), WavPack (−1.5 pp) and APE (−0.3 pp) on identical
material; loses to OptimFROG (−2.1 pp) and TAK (−0.6 pp). The LPC/Rice core
is real — not just the container.

## Coverage — the other half of the story

| Tool | accepted | rejected |
|---|---|---|
| FLQ | **148/148** | 0 |
| WavPack | 148/148 | 0 |
| Monkey's Audio | 148/148 | 0 |
| 7-Zip / Zstd / PAQ8PX | 148/148 | 0 |
| FLAC | 79/148 | 69 (float WAV, AIFF, odd headers) |
| OptimFROG | 73/142* | 69 (float, non-canonical) |
| TAK | 48/142* | 94 (wav-only + strict header rules) |

*OFR/TAK are wav-only tools; rejections include float WAVs and
non-canonical RIFF headers (`UNEXPECTEDEOF`, `Audio format not supported`).
These freesound files are real-world messy: float64/32 stems, odd chunks.

PAQ8PX's WAV model lands at ~49–66% depending on file — strong on
repetitive material but not uniformly dominant; ~140× slower than FLAC.

## Takeaways

1. FLQ's codec core is legitimately competitive: #3 of 6 audio codecs on
   identical inputs, behind only the two ratio-focused veterans (OFR, TAK).
2. Its edge is coverage + versatility (float WAVs, AIFF, weird headers),
   plus joint refs on top — none of the reference codecs handle this corpus
   fully.
3. Honest weaknesses: encode is ~4–80× slower than the reference codecs
   (self+cross analysis pass; ~5.7 s/file vs FLAC's ~0.07 s), decode is
   fine (~0.2 s/file). 7-Zip/Zstd lose to every audio codec on PCM —
   format-aware coding beats generic LZMA/zstd by 8–20 pp.
4. PAQ8PX stays the "extreme" reference only by theory: on real WAVs its
   ratio is merely good while being ~2,000× slower to encode.

Raw data: sweep script + CSV live in `D:\TEMP\flq_ab\` (outside repo by
policy). Repro: `python D:\TEMP\flq_ab\bench.py`.


## Ablation (encoder attribution, same 47 files)

To separate the codec core from the encoder's extra decisions, each file was
re-encoded with `flq encode` (full) and `flq encode --no-joint` (reference
analysis skipped). The stats table exposes the pipeline stages directly;
both containers decode byte-exact for all 47 files.

FLQ pipeline stages (payload bytes, % of input):

| Stage | Ratio | Median |
|---|---|---|
| L0 independent per-channel LPC/Rice | 50.95% | 52.67% |
| L1 + stereo decorrelation | 50.77% | 51.60% |
| L2 + self/cross references (full FLQ) | 50.51% | 51.13% |

So on single unrelated files the LPC/Rice core alone is already ahead of
FLAC-file-level output; stereo transforms and reference coding add ~0.4 pp
combined here (references matter much more on related multi-file bundles).

Audio stream vs container (does the container tax the comparison?):

| Component | Size | Ratio |
|---|---|---|
| FLQ audio payload | 337.4 MiB | 50.51% |
| FLQ .flq total | 337.4 MiB | 50.51% (overhead ~0.008%) |
| FLAC stream | 341.3 MiB | 51.09% |
| FLAC file | 341.7 MiB | 51.15% |
| WavPack stream | 346.7 MiB | 51.89% |
| WavPack file | 347.6 MiB | 52.04% |

Pairwise per-file wins/losses vs FLQ total (median delta in pp of input):

| Competitor | Win | Loss | Median |
|---|---|---|---|
| FLAC | 44 | 3 | +0.66 |
| WavPack | 36 | 11 | +1.09 |
| OptimFROG | 5 | 42 | -1.59 |
| TAK | 9 | 38 | -0.55 |
| APE | 24 | 23 | +0.01 |
| 7-Zip | 41 | 6 | +14.26 |
| Zstd | 44 | 3 | +25.86 |

Read: the FLAC and WavPack leads are statistically solid; APE is a
coin-flip on this subset (median delta +0.01 pp, p25 -0.43); OFR and TAK
stay ahead. Even the bare LPC/Rice stage (L0) beats FLAC 32:15 and WavPack
31:16 per file - the core itself is competitive, not just the container.

Cost attribution: full encode 457.7 s vs no-joint 152.6 s - reference
analysis is ~2/3 of encode time for +0.26 pp on this subset.
